DILG BACONC PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.diiq.gov.ph OIL G HON. LEONEL D. CENIZA Municipal Mayor Municipality of Pantukan Municipal Hall, Townsite, Kingking Pantukan, Province of Davao de Oro Dear Mayor Ceniza: This has reference to your letter dated 21 June 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion on the application of EO 41 or the collection of road toll upon Hexat Mining Corporation's truck transporting mineral ores via municipal road. Per the representation, the Sangguniang Bayan of Pantukan enacted Ordinance No. 155 series of 2023 on June 7, 2023 amending tax ordinance No. 01 series of 2017 which effectively amended the existing tax ordinance of the Municipality of Pantukan. You then claimed that since the ordinance took effect, the Municipality has been collecting road tolls from the operators of the vehicles covered by it. You also stated that Hexat Mining Corporation, a firm that performs mining operations and exploration in Sitio Diat, Barangay Napnapan, Pantukan, Davao de Oro, is among those that paid the road tolls mandated by the Ordinance. You likewise mentioned that the mineral ores and geological materials Hexat extracts are transported from Barangay Napnapan to Tagum City via Tibagon — Diat, Napnapan Road, a Municipal Road of Pantukan. You then cited this Department's letter dated March 6, 2024 to Mr. Ferdinand Galang, President of Hexat where this Department opined that the term "goods and merchandise" mentioned in EO 41 covers all kinds of goods which includes the delivery of mineral ores in its respective trucking routes, only subject to the nature of the road to which it traverses. You then claimed that Hexat was dishonest in withholding critical facts such as the fact that the subject road is a Municipal Road, and that the Municipality of Pantukan maintains this road and has done so since before Hexat built a portion of it. Accordingly, it is your position that Hexat must pay the road toll imposed by Ordinance No. 155, series of 2023 and that Hexat is not covered by the EO No. 41 because the prohibition only applies to national roads and other roads not constructed and funded by LGUs pursuant to Section 155 of RA No. 7160. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Furthermore, you stated that EO No. 41 does not apply to the Tibagon-Diat, Napnapan Road because it is not a national road. Rather, it is a municipal road owned and maintained by the municipality. Thus, the request for legal opinion on whether Hexat should pay road toll as provided by the Municipal Ordinance No. 155, series of 2023. At the onset, please be informed that this issue has long been settled by the Department. As previously opined under DILG Legal Opinion Nos. 16, 19, 59 s. 2012, hereunder is our discussion on the issue, viz: Pass through fees are taxes, fees, charges and other impositions upon goods carried into or out of, or passing through the territorial jurisdiction of the LGUs in the guise of a toll, charges for wharfage or other taxes, fees, or charges in any form upon goods or merchandise. Local ordinances imposing/collecting taxes, fees or charges are considered illegal and run counter to Sec. 133 (e) of the Code. Notably, Sec. 133 of the Code enumerates the common limitations on the taxing powers of the local government units. Nevertheless, LGUs may regulate the use of its road or other public facilities as provided under Sec. 155 of the Code through the imposition of toll fees or charges thereon provided that is funded and constructed by the local government unit concerned, viz: Sec. 155. Toll Fees or Charges. The Sanggunian concerned may prescribe the terms and conditions and fix the rates for the imposition of toll fees or charges for the use of any public road, pier or wharf, waterway, bridge, ferry or telecommunication system funded and constructed by the local government unit concerned: Provided, That no such toll fees or charges shall be collected from officers and enlisted men of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and members of the Philippine National Police on mission, post office personnel delivering mail, physically-handicapped, and disabled citizens who are sixty-five (65) years or older. When public safety and welfare so requires, the Sanggunian concerned may discontinue the collection of the tolls, and thereafter the said facility shall be free and open for public use. Please note that DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2011-122 was issued by the Department to deter LGUs from imposing and collecting fees, taxes, charges and other impositions which are beyond its taxing powers pursuant to Sec. 133 (e) of the Code. This does not cover other LGU impositions which are authorized by the Code such as the imposition of toll fees under Sec. 155. Regarding the imposition of EO 41 on municipal roads, please be advised that this was also resolved in the previously cited letter to Mr. Galang, in which the Department stated that the Municipality of Pantukan may collect fees or charges for the use of the subject roads because the Municipality owns and maintains such roads. Section I of EO 41 states unequivocally that the prohibition applies exclusively to national roads and other roads that are not constructed and funded by LGUs under Section 155 of RA No. 7160. Page 2 of 3

Nonetheless, we ought to emphasize that the same presidential issuance encourages the deferment of collection/imposition of said fees in connection with LGU-funded and constructed roads. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, Under RITY OF THE SECRETAR N VI OR R. LLAMAS retary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OU LAJJVRULLLS-LRALLD/lasm Page 3 of 3
